page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.large is an entry-tier virtual server instance powered by AMD EPYC processors on the KVM hypervisor. Configured with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs operating at a nominal clock frequency of 2.25 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per virtual core. The server configuration includes 1 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and comes without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Because local disk storage is not bundled with the instance, external network-attached block storage is required for persistent root filesystems and data volumes. The system also contains zero discrete GPU accelerators. The use of dedicated vCPU allocation avoids CPU oversubscription penalties, offering consistent operational predictability across both cores. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio enforces strict ceiling limits on resident memory, trading substantial in-memory caching capacity for a compact compute footprint.

The ecs.u2a-c1m2.large configuration provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for workloads characterized by moderate processing demands and low memory footprints. Typical applications include lightweight web serving, containerized microservices, development and staging servers, continuous integration build runners, and background batch tasks that function reliably within the 4.0 GB memory limit.
